what_happened: Gate 20's budget overage cited in the task description (eager-load 71712B vs 70400B baseline) is already resolved as of this dispatch: live 'verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 20' run shows all 4 sub-checks PASS (eager-load exactly at baseline 70400B, commands/orchestrate.md 21496/21500B, SKILL.md 25692/26000B). Intervening tasks 620 and 634 (commits 0984f635f, c3f838fae, landed before this dispatch) already closed the SKILL.md ceiling finding that produced the cited overage. No trim/rebaseline is strictly required to pass the gate today; the remaining question is whether to add real headroom given the config's own history of ~10 reactive razor-thin-margin ceiling moves.

Task 607's second question (per-gate timeout should scale with observed concurrency) substantially overlaps task 610 (full_gate_verification_ceiling_and_stall, not_started, created one day after 607)'s own research question 4 ('Should per-gate bounds scale with measured host load... so a load-induced kill is mechanically distinguishable from a real failure'). 610's duplicate-check (run after 607 already existed) did not surface 607, and 607's own duplicate-check (run before 610 existed) could not have surfaced 610 either -- an undetected near-duplicate, unflagged in either task's audit_verdict or description. Recommend keeping 607's remedy narrow (raise/confirm specific empirically-tight timeout_s values) and leaving the general load-adaptive-timeout mechanism design to 610, with a cross-reference added to avoid duplicate future work.

Task description's claim that 'gates 8 and 10... were killed by their own 60s per-gate timeout' does not match gate-registry.data: gate 8 (tests/run-all.sh) declares timeout_s=1500, not 60s, and no corroborating incident of gate 8 itself being killed by a 60s timeout was found anywhere in specs/*/issues.jsonl or handoffs. Gate 10 (validate-state.sh --deep, timeout_s=60) IS independently corroborated three times (specs/562's issues.jsonl x2, specs/634's issues.jsonl x1, all 2026-11-16, all re-passing standalone in 61-66s under ~load 11/24 cores). Sibling task 610's own description additionally names gates 3 and 4 (doc-lint, task-ref lint, both timeout_s=60) as hit in one earlier batch. Recommend the remedy target the corroborated set (gate 10, and gates 3/4 if reproduced) rather than gate 8.

validate-artifact.sh's suite-selection advisory caught an under-verifying Tier Justification on Phase 2 at authoring time: it named test-gate-registry-resolution.sh alone, while suite_selection_select returns 10 suites for gate-registry.data/known-failures.txt (including test-gate-cache-lib.sh case 10, which asserts a timeout_s row edit changes the gate implementation digest). Fixed before the plan was returned.

gate-registry.data's timeout_s field documentation states the value is derived from gate-cost-model.csv's clean avg_ms at ~3x headroom, but that mechanically-generated CSV currently carries exactly one data row (gate8). No avg_ms exists for gates 3/4/10, so the documented derivation rule cannot be applied; the plan derives 180s from corroborated incident evidence instead and records the deviation. Regenerating the model is excluded (gate8 alone measured 662s per run, twice).

This plan's Phase 2 edit target agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/gate-registry.data is inside concurrent sibling task 584's declared file_scope (584 is at research phase this same cycle). Low risk since a research dispatch writes a report, not source-store scripts, but Phase 2 opens with a mandatory re-read-and-stop-on-foreign-modification step per the territory contract.

Phase 1's targeted suite run (test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) failed its baseline-fixture-clean case for a DIFFERENT underlying reason than the one named in known-failures.txt's declared row (gate24 /ide finding): with the source-store edit not yet redeployed, the live repo's own gate5 content-hash check flags orchestrator-context-budget.json as differing from its deployed mirror, which alone makes the fixture's full verify-deploy run return rc=1. run-all.sh's own EXPECTED/NEW classification matches purely by suite name, not by which finding caused the failure, so it correctly reported '0 NEW' despite the cause mismatch. This is the exact gate5-red-during-source-edit state the plan's own Risks table anticipated for phases 1-2, resolved by Phase 3's redeploy. Noting as a minor classification blind spot (known-failures.txt attribution can go stale about WHY a suite fails even while correctly tracking WHETHER it is expected), not a regression.

Phase 2's targeted suite run showed test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh failing with 'gate4 (gate4_run) exceeded its 60s timeout and was killed', not the gate10 failure known-failures.txt's row describes -- because this suite's cold-baseline fixture uses 'git worktree add --detach HEAD', which checks out only COMMITTED history and so still saw the pre-Phase-2 60s timeout_s values (the gate-registry.data raise was uncommitted at verification time). run-all.sh's suite-name-only EXPECTED/NEW classification correctly reported 0 NEW despite the different proximate gate/cause, consistent with the Phase 1 nuance already logged. This also confirms the fixture is immune to in-flight uncommitted edits by construction (relevant to the territory/concurrency risk the plan's own Risks table named for this file), and predicts that a FUTURE re-run of this suite after Phase 2's commit will exercise the new 180s bound instead.

Phase 3's redeploy (deploy-headless.sh) landed cleanly for this task's own three edited files (orchestrator-context-budget.json, gate-registry.data, known-failures.txt -- all three manually diff-confirmed source==deployed, silent), and gate 20 (budget, widened bounds) and gate 10 (state schema) both PASS via verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 5,10,20 --skip-unchanged. Gate 5 (content-hash equality) FAILS, but its 4 findings are ALL on files outside task 607's declared file_scope: context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md, scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh, scripts/orchestrate-build-aux-dispatch.sh, scripts/tests/test-runtime-file-tracking.sh. git log timestamps show these were committed by concurrent sibling tasks (core: add the gate cache and gate mutex..., core: name the real carrier the blocker-research chain reads, core: add the three missing library suites...) at 2026-11-18T14:33-14:39, landing in the narrow window around this task's own deploy-headless.sh invocation (14:41) -- a deploy-vs-concurrent-commit race, not a regression from this task's edits. Per Stage 3.6 Observation Duty, reporting rather than fixing: this task's file_scope does not cover those four files, and the full gate set is deferred to the batch's own close sweep per the dispatch's Batch Gate Deferral directive, which will naturally pick up the now-settled commits on its next redeploy.
